rules.quote: If there is no snow before January, there will be the more in March and April.
March in Janiveer, Janiveer in March, I fear.
A warm January, a cold May.
If St. Paul's Day be fine, the year will be the same.
February fill dyke; March lick it out.
If February give much snow, a fine summer it doth foreshow.
Whenever the latter part of February and beginning of March are dry, there will be a deficiency of rain up to Midsummer Day.
For every thunder with rain in February there will be a cold spell in May.
As long as the sunbeam comes in on Bridget's feast-day, the snow comes before May Day.
If Marie's purifying dale be cleare and bright with sunnie raie, then frost and cold shall be much more after the feast.
As far as the sun shines in on Candlemas Day, So far will the snow blow in afore old May.
Should the sun shine out at the Purification, there will be more ice after the festival than there was before it.
If Candlemas Day bring clouds and rain, Winter is gone and won't come again.
If a storm on February 2nd, spring is near.
If that day be bright and clear, the spring will be late.
When drops hang on the fence on February 2nd, icicles will hang thereon March 25th.
If the eighteen last days of February be wet, and the first ten of March, the spring quarter and summer too will prove too wet.
If cold at St. Peter's Day, it will last longer (shows weather for next forty days).
If it freezes on St. Matthias' Day, it will freeze for a month together.
St. Matthias breaks the ice; if he finds none, he will make it.
March comes in like a lion and goes out like a lamb.
March comes in like a lamb and goes out like a lion.
So many frosts in March, so many in May.
As it rains in March, so it rains in June.
High winds on these days [borrowing days, late March], a dry summer to follow
After a wet April a dry June.
If the first three days of April be foggy, there will be a flood in June.
A dry May is followed by a wet June.
Wet May, dry July.
If May be cold and wet, September will be warm and dry, and vice-versa.
If May be cold and wet, September will be warm and dry, and vice-versa.
Storms from the east or south-east, between 17th and 23rd of March, indicate a wet summer.
A wet June makes a dry September.
If it rain on June 8th (St. Medard), it will rain forty days later.
If it rain on June 19th (St. Protais), it rains for forty days after.
If St. Vitus's Day be rainy weather, it will rain for thirty days together.
When it is hottest in June, it will be coldest in the corresponding days of the next February.
If it rains on June 27th, it will rain seven weeks.
If the 1st of July it be rainy weather, It will rain more or less for four weeks together.
If it rains on St. Mary's Day, it will rain for four weeks.
If it rains on first dog-day, it will rain for forty days after.
Bullion's Day, gif ye be fair, For forty days 'twill rain nae mair.
If it rains on July 10th, it will rain for seven weeks.
When the months of July, August, and September are unusually hot, January will be the coldest month.
If St. Swithin weep, that year, the proverb says, The weather will be foul for forty days.
St. Swithin's Day, an ye be fair, For forty days 'twill rain nae mair
Thunderstorms in the beginning of August will generally be followed by others all the month.
If the first week in August is unusually warm, the winter will be white and long.
If on St. Lawrence's Day the weather be fine, fair autumn and good wine may be hoped for.
If this day be misty, the morning beginning with a hoar-frost, the cold weather will soon come, and a hard winter.
If it rains this day, it will rain the forty days after.
When September has been rainy, the following May is generally dry
When May is dry, the following September is apt to be wet
A wet September, drought for next summer
If the storms in September clear off warm, all the storms of the following winter will be warm.
When a cold spell occurs in September and passes without a frost, a frost will not occur until the same time in October.
Fair on September 1st, fair for the month.
If the hart and the hind meet dry and part dry on Rood Day fair, for sax weeks, of rain there'll be nae mail.
If it does not rain on St. Michael's and Gallus, a dry spring is indicated for the next year.
When it freezes and snows in October, January will bring mild weather.
If October bring heavy frosts and winds, then will January and February be mild.
Warm October, cold February.
October and November cold indicate that the following January and February will be mild and dry.
October and November cold indicate that the following January and February will be mild and dry.
If there's ice in November that will bear a duck. There'll be nothing after but sludge and muck.
Ice in November brings mud in December.
If All Saints' Day will bring out the winter, St. Martin's Day will bring out Indian summer.
If this day (All Saints') be fair, the next winter will bring but little rain and snow along with it.
If ducks do swim at Hollantide, At Christmas they will slide.
If the geese at Martin's Day stand on ice, they will walk in mud at Christmas.
As at Catherine foul or fair, so will be the next February.
As at Catherine foul or fair, so will be the next February.
Frost on the shortest day is said to indicate a severe winter.
If ice will bear a man before Christmas, it will not bear a mouse afterwards.
If it rain much during the twelve days after Christmas, it will be a wet year.
As the equinoctial storms clear, so will all storms clear for the six months.
